NVDA - NVIDIA’S HUANG REJECTS CALLS TO SLOW AI Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says AI development should move “as fast as we can,” rejecting calls for the industry to slow down. Huang stressed that speed should not come at the expense of safety, as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warns rapid AI advances may require greater caution and safeguards.

HORMUZ OIL FLOWS HIT SIX-MONTH HIGH Oil and LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have reached their highest level in six months, as U.S. mine-clearing and naval protection efforts boost tanker traffic. CENTCOM says Gulf allies have moved more than 1 billion barrels of crude through the strait in recent months.

U.S., DENMARK AND GREENLAND REACH SECURITY DEAL The U.S., Denmark and Greenland have agreed to expand America’s military presence in Greenland, with signing expected next week at the UN General Assembly. Denmark and Greenland insist the agreement will not compromise Greenland’s sovereignty, despite Trump saying Washington will have “permanent control” over the island’s security. Key details of the deal remain unclear.

WHITE HOUSE ENFORCES BAN ON CNN, MS NOW AND POLITICO The White House confiscated press passes and denied access to journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico, following through on Trump’s announced ban. All three outlets say they will defend their First Amendment rights, signaling potential legal challenges.

U.S.-CHINA TALKS SET AHEAD OF TRUMP-XI SUMMIT Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will meet Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng on Sunday in New York to discuss AI security, trade and broader economic issues. The talks come just days before Trump hosts Xi Jinping at the White House, setting the stage for high-level U.S.-China negotiations.

TRUMP: “VERY BIG THINGS” COMING ON IRAN President Trump says he is in “a deciding mode” on Iran, warning that “very big things” could happen in the not-so-distant future. Trump said the options range from further military action to economic pressure or a deal, while adding he would probably be open to meeting Iran’s president at the UN.

TIER 2 IRAN WARNS NEW U.S. ATTACK MAY BE COMING, THREATENS SUSTAINED RETALIATION Iran says it has information that the U.S. and allies are preparing a major new attack, Reuters reported. Tehran’s military command warned any strike would trigger sustained retaliation against U.S. bases and interests and could make regional U.S. allies parties to the conflict; it provided no evidence for the claimed preparations.
